about: Generic labware a workflow can be run in (issue #53). Nothing here names a product. 'maxUl' is the nominal capacity of one well or tube for the labware class, not a working volume: confirm it for the exact product. 'format' is how the engine counts work (once per plate, or once per tube). 'mentions' are words in protocol text that name a different kind of container; when a protocol uses them, the Decide page asks whether running it in this labware is a method change. No catalogue record says which decks or modules accept which labware, so every fit is a question for the instrument owner. 'pylabrobot' says which PyLabRobot resource definitions (content/pylabrobot-labware.json) are instances of each type, by geometry: resource types, well count, bottom types, plate height and PyLabRobot's brim-to-bottom well volume (geometric, larger than the working volume).
basis: nominal capacity for the labware class; confirm for the exact product

physical.about: Physical-state ledger (#120): the containers a run fills, draws from and empties, and the rules the ledger applies, for handlers with no PyLabRobot deck recorded in content/pylabrobot-export.json (those use their PyLabRobot resources' capacities). Generic classes, assumed: confirm against the reservoirs you use.

channelFit.basis: Independent channels are spread at least 9 mm apart and kept clear of the cavity walls. Edge clearance fitted to PyLabRobot at the pinned commit, which takes 8 channels into a 72 mm trough but not a 71.2 mm one (#111). Fixed blocks are not checked: their spacing is built for the reservoirs they use.

reservoir.label: 12-column reservoir
reservoir.basis: assumed: a 12-column reservoir of 15 ml per column, as in PyLabRobot's NEST definitions

trough.label: single-well reservoir
trough.basis: assumed: a single-well reservoir of 195 ml, as in PyLabRobot's NEST definitions

waste.label: liquid waste reservoir
waste.basis: assumed: a single-well reservoir of 195 ml used for liquid waste
